State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 
 In The Court Of Ms. Neha Gupta Singh
 Chief Judicial Magistrate
 North District, Rohini, Delhi
State Vs. Kuldeep Singh
Fir No : 264/2011
P. S. : Alipur
U/s : 279/338/304A Ipc
 Judgment
Registration No. of the case : 5283953/2016 Date of its institution : 06.03.2012 Name of the complainant : Yogesh Date of Commission of offence : 31.07.2011 Name of the accused : Kuldeep Singh S/o Sh. Om Prakash R/o Village Bushan, Tehsil Tosham, District Bhiwani,Haryana Offence complained of : U/s 279/338/304A IPC Plea of accused : pleaded not guilty Case reserved for orders : 21.06.2024 Date of judgment : 04.07.2024 Final Order : Accused is acquitted for offence u/s 279/338/304A IPC BRIEF STATEMENT OF FACTS FOR THE DECISION :-
1. The prosecution story in brief is that on 31.07.2011 at about 11.25 am at Satyawadi Raja Harish Chander hospital chowk, near DSIDC and B-4, Alipur, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Alipur, accused was found driving a Tata-407 bearing registration no. HR-61-A-3434 in a rash and negligent manner at public place so as to endagner human life and personal safety of others. Further, accused caused grievous injuries to Yogesh S/o Sh. Subodh Yadav CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No.
264/11 PS Alipur 1 of 17 and accused also caused death of one Gokul S/o Sh. Rudha Ram and the present FIR was registered. 
2. Investigation was completed and charge sheet was filed under section 279/338/304A IPC. Cognizance was taken and accused was summoned. 
3. Copy of charge sheet and documents were supplied to the accused in compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C.
4. Arguments on Notice were heard and Notice against accused Kuldeep Singh was framed under section 279/338/304A IPC and accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, prosecution examined following witnesses.
6. PW-1 Sh. Raghubir Singh deposed that on 01.08.2011, he was present in his house and he received a call from PS Alipur regarding accident of his brother-in-law namely Gokul Ram and thereafter he went to BJRM hospital and identified dead body of his State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
1 brother-in-law and after postmortem, dead body was handed over vide handing over memo Ex. PW-1/A. This witness was not cross examined despite opportunity being given. 
7. PW-2 Sh. Vijay Singh deposed that on 01.08.2011, he was present in his house and he was informed by his brother- in-law i.e. Sh. Raghubir Singh about accident of his CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No.
264/11 PS Alipur 2 of 17 brother namely Gokul Ram and thereafter they went to BJRM hospital and identified dead body of his brother and after postmortem, dead body was handed over to them vide handing over memo Ex. PW-1/A. This witness was not cross examined despite opportunity being given. 
8. PW-3 Sh. Sanjit deposed that 31.07.2011 he was present in his house and he received a call from police station regarding accident of his tempo bearing registration no. HR 61A-3034 and police served him a Notice u/s 133 MV Act and he filed reply on the same from point A to A-1 which is Ex.
PW-3/A. He further deposed that on the day of incident, the vehicle was being driven by his brother i.e. accused Kuldeep Singh. He also deposed that he got the vehicle released on superdari vide superdarinama i.e. Ex. PW-3/B. He also identified the vehicle i.e. HR 61A-3034 and he also correctly identified four photographs i.e. Ex. P- 1 (colly.). This witness was duly cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused. 
9. PW-4Ct. Devender Kumar deposed that on 31.07.2011, DD No. 35B regarding accident was marked to SI Devender Balhar and accordingly, he alongwith him went to the spot i.e. SRHC Hospital chowk near DSIDC and B- 4, Alipur, Delhi and found two vehicles i.e. tempo bearing No.
HR 61 A 3034 and motorcycle bearing no. DL 8SAU- 0219 in accidental condition and one dead body was also lying on the spot. He further deposed that they came to know that one injured had shifted to hospital and SI CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 3 of 17 Devender Balhara left him on the spot and went to SRHC hospital and after some time, SI Devender reached back at the spot and prepared one tehrir and handed over the same to him for registration of FIR and accordingly, he left the spot and went to PS Alipur for registration of FIR and after getting FIR registered, he came back at the spot and handed over copy of FIR and original tehrir to SI Rajender Singh from MACT Cell, who was present alongwith Ct. Inderjeet at the spot at that time. 
He further deposed that IO prepared one application for preservation of dead body and handed over to him and asked him to go at BJRM hospital, Jahangir Puri alongwith the application and thereafter he gave the application and got preserved the dead body at mortuary. He further deposed that on 01.08.2011 IO reached at hospital and got conducted the postmortem of the dead body of deceased Gokul and thereafter he relieved from there. He correctly identified tempo bearing no. HR 61A-3034 in photographs Ex. P-1 (colly.). He also correctly identified the spot in photographs Ex.
P-2 (colly.). This witness was duly cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused. 
10.PW-5 ASI Balak Ram deposed that on 31.07.2011, he was posted as Duty Officer at PS Alipur and on that day at about 2:40pm, he received a rukka from Ct. Devender, sent by SI Devender and on the basis of rukka, he registered FIR No. 264/11 and copy of which is Ex. PW-5/A and his State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
2 andorsement on rukka is Ex. PW-5/B and after registration of FIR, he handed over the copy of FIR to Ct. Devender to CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 4 of 17 hand over the same to SI Rajender. This witness was not cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused depsite opportunity being given. 
11.PW-6 ASI/ Tech (Retd.) Devender Kumar deposed that he was qualified Grade-I Mechanic and he had done specialized course/training in Automobile and Vehicle Mechanic from ITI and various vehicles manufacturing companies and he had been doing mechanical inspection work from last 30 years. He further deposed that on 02.08.2011, he conducted mechanical inspection in respect of vehicle i.e. one motorcycle bearing no. DL 8SAU-0219 and one Tata 407 tempo bearing no.
HR-61A-3034 at the request of IO SI Rajender Singh vide inspection reports i.e. Ex. PW-6/A and Ex. PW-6/B and he stated that there were fresh damages on both the vehicles while motorcycle was found not fit for road test but the Tata-407 tempo was fit for road test. This witness was not cross examined depsite opportunity being given. 
12.PW-7 Sh. Yogesh deposed that he was working as a Muneem in a Daal Mill in Bhorgarh, Narela,
Delhi and on 30.07.2011 at about 8:30-8:45 am, he alongwith his colleague Gokul, who was also working as Muneem in the same Daal Mill, were returning to Mill from Narela on a motorcycle no.
DL- 8SAU-0219 Bajaj Platinum, driven by him. He further deposed that when they reached on the way going towards B-4, Punjabi Colony from chowk, SRHC hospital, they were on left side of the road and CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 5 of 17 suddenly, one tempo bearing no. 3034 came from front side at a very high speed and it was overtaking other vehicle in negligent manner and hit their motorcycle from front side. He further deposed that after accident, they fell on the road alongwith motorcycle and they sustained injuries. Thereafter, the offending tempo stopped and driver of the offending tempo got down and after seeing them in injured condition, he ran away from the spot after leaving the offending tempo on the spot. He further deposed that thereafter he became unconscious and PCR officials took them to SRHC hospital and he regained his consciousness in the hospital and police recorded his statement i.e. Ex.
PW-7/A. He further deposed that he came to know that his colleague Gokul had expired in the accident and the accused accompanied the police to SRHC hospital and he had identified him as driver of offending vehicle in the hospital. He further deposed that police arrested the accused vide arrest memo Ex. PW-7/B and he had informed about the place of accident to the police. He also admitted that complete registration number of the offending vehicle as HR-61A-3034 and he also correctly identified the offending vehicle in photographs alongwith negatives Ex. P-1 (colly.). He also correctly identified accused/driver of offending vehicle in the court. This witness was duly cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused. 
13.PW-8 Ct. Inderjeet Singh deposed that on 31.07.2011 he was posted at AIU/MACT Cell, Sector-3,
Rohini, Delhi and on that day, IO received DD No. 8 regarding an CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 6 of 17 accident and on receipt of the said DD, he alongwith IO went to the spot i.e. near SRHC hospital, where SI Devender alongwith one constable met them and handed over custody of driver of offending vehicle namely Kuldeep Singh. He further deposed that at the spot, one motorcycle Bajaj Platinum bearing no. DL-8SAU-0219 and one Swaraj Mazda bearing no. HR-61A-3034 was found in accidental condition and IO seized both the vehicles vide State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
3 seizure memos Ex. PW-8/A and Ex. PW-8/B. He further deposed that injured namely Yogesh came to the spot and narrated his statement and IO recorded his statement and prepared rukka and Ct. 
Devender went to the police station, got the FIR registered and returned to the spot. He further deposed that IO prepared site plan at the instance of injured Yogesh i.e. Ex. PW-7/D-1 and IO also arrested the accused vide memo Ex. PW-7/B and personally searched the accused vide memo Ex.
PW-8/C and IO also seized Permit and other documents of vehicle vide memo Ex. PW-8/E and case property and accused were sent to police station. He further deposed that on the next day i.e.
01.08.2011, he alongwith IO went to BJRM hospital, where IO recorded dead body identification statement i.e. Ex. PW-8/F and Ex. PW-8/G and after postmortem, dead body was handed over to relatives of deceased vide memo Ex. PW-1/A. He correctly identified photographs of case property as Ex. P-1 and Ex. P-2 (colly.). He also correctly identified accused Kuldeep in the court. This witness was not cross examined by the accused despite opportunity being given. CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 7 of 17 14.PW-9 Dr. Rajesh Kumar, Sr Medical Officer, SRHC hospital correctly identified signatures and handwriting of Dr. Mazhar Hussain on MLC No. 856/11 dated 31.07.2011 which is Ex. PW-9/A and signatures of Dr. Mazhar Hussain at point A. This witness was not cross examined by the accused despite opportunity being given. 
15.PW-10 SI Devender Singh deposed that on 31.07.2011, he was posted at PS Alipur as SI and on that day, he received DD No. 35B regarding accident and on receipt of said DD, he alongwith Ct.
Devender went to the spot i.e. SRHC chowk, where one Tata tempo no. HR 61A-3034 and one motorcycle Bajaj Platia bearing no. DL 8CAU-0219 found in accidental condition. He further deposed that one person was also found dead at the spot and he came to know that one another injured had been shifted to the hospital and leaving Ct. Devender at the spot, he went to SRHC hospital, where he found admitted injured Yogesh and doctor declared him fit for statement therefore, he recorded his statement which is Ex. PW-7/A. He further deposed that he returned on the spot and he prepared rukka Ex. PW- 10/A and rukka was sent to police station through Ct.
Devender for registration of FIR and he went to police station, got the FIR registered and returned at the spot alongwith SI Rajender and he handed over copy of FIR and rukka to him. He further deposed that he handed over custody of both vehicles to SI Rajender, who recorded his statement. 
He correctly identified photographs alongwith CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No.
264/11 PS Alipur 8 of 17 negatives already attached with judicial file as Ex. P-1 and Ex. P-2 (colly.).
This witness was duly cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused.
16.PW-11 SI (Retd.) Rajender deposed that on 31.07.2011, he was posted as AIU OD as SI and on that day, he had received DD No. 8 i.e. Ex. PW-11/A regarding an accident and on receipt of said DD, he alongwith Ct. Inderjeet went to the spot, where two vehicles i.e. tempo and motorcycle found in accidental condition. He further deposed that Ct. Inderjeet reached at the spot and handed over copy of FIR and rukka to him and he got clicked the photographs of the spot and injured Yogesh also reached at the spot after visiting the hospital. He further deposed that he prepared site plan at his instance i.e. Ex. PW-7/D1 and he also served Notice u/s 133 MV Act to the registered owner of the offending tempo vide memo Ex. PW-11/B and registered owner replied that brother of the accused was the driver and he seized Driving Licence of the accused vide memo Ex. PW-8/D and also seized State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
4 motorcycle and tempo vide memos Ex. PW-8/A and Ex. PW-8/B. He further deposed that he arrested and personally searched the accused vide memo Ex. PW-7/B and Ex. PW-8/C and he recorded statements of witnesses and he also got conducted mechanical inspection of both the vehicles. He further deposed that he went to BJRM mortuary on 01.08.2011 and got conducted postmortem of deceased and he recorded statement of dead body identification i.e. Ex. PW-8/F and Ex. PW-8/G and handed over dead body of CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 9 of 17 deceased to relative of deceased vide memo i.e. Ex. PW- 7/A. He further deposed that he seized documents of temps vide memo Ex. PW-8/E and he also got verified the documents of the offending vehicle and he recorded statements of witnesses and prepared the chargesheet and filed the same before the court. He correctly identified photographs of the spot and case property as Ex. P-1 and Ex. P-2 (colly.). This witness was duly cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused. 
17.PW-12 Sh. Shashi Bhushan Kumar, Record Clerk of Dr. Mukesh Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre,
Narela deposed that he was working as a Record Clerk and as per record, X-ray plates/film of injured Yogesh Yadav are not available in the hospital and he had mentioned about non availability of X-ray plate/film on the letter head of Dr. Mukesh Orthopaedic and Traume Centre, Narela, Delhi which is Ex. PW-12/A. He further deposed that Dr. Mukesh Aggarwal had conducted X-ray of patient Yogesh Yadav and on 28.04.2021, Dr. Mukesh Aggarwal passed away in the second wave of Covid-19 and death certificate of Dr. Mukesh Aggarwal is marked as Mark-A-1. This witness was not cross examined by the accused despite opportunity being given. 
18.PW-13 Sh. Satish Kumar, Mortuary Attendant, BJRM hospital has proved record of postmortem report No. 704/2011 dated 01.08.2011 of deceased by Dr. V.K. Ranga, HoD. He further identified handwriting and signatures of CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 10 of 17 Dr. Vivek Rawat at point A on postmortem report No. 704/2011 dated 01.08.2011 which is Ex.
PW-13/A. This witness was not cross examined by Ld counsel for the accused despite opportunity being given. 
19.PW-14 Sh. Mohit Mittal deposed that he is the Superdar of motorcycle registered in the name of M/s. Kanha Keshav Foods at H-1650/51, DSIIDC, Narela Industrial, Delhi and he was also partner in the company. He further deposed that on 30.08.2011, he got released the motorcycle on superdari vide supardarinama i.e. Ex. PW-14/A. He further deposed that he could not bring the motorcycle in the court as it was not in working condition, however he brought photographs of the said motorcycle and the said photograph are Ex. X-1 (colly.).
20.In his statement recorded on 09.06.2017 , accused did not dispute the identity of vehicle during the trial. 
21.Thereafter, prosecution evidence was closed by the order of the court. Statement of accused was recorded under Section 313Cr.P.C. All the incriminating evidences were put to the accused, to which he stated that he is innocent, he was not driving in rash and negligent manner. He wished to lead defense evidence. 
22.In his defence, accused has examined one witness. 
State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
5 23.DW-1 Sh. Sunil deposed that on 31.07.2011 at about 6:00 am, driver namely Kuldeep Singh of vehicle make Tata CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 11 of 17 tempo bearing no. 3034 made a call to him and informed that he had suffered with an accident with one cow on road and he also told him that when he was driving the said vehicle, the said cow suddenly came in front of his vehicle on the road and he could applied brakes and accident took place at Satyawadi Harish Chand chowk near DSIDC and B-4, Alipur, Delhi. He further deposed that he apprised him to call insurance company and also directed him to get the vehicle parked at one side of the road and thereafter, he reached at the said spot at about 7:00 am and he saw one white colour car was plying on the road and he hit against one motorcyclist and after the said accident, driver of the said car alongwith the car fled away from there. He further deposed that some public persons gathered at the spot and someone called the police and thereafter police reached at the spot and the said injured motorcyclist was taken to the hospital and at that time, there were two persons on the motorcycle. He further deposed that at that time, one injured was seemed unconscious and other was found conscious and police officials made inquiries from the said publilc persons and asked about the registration number of the said offending car and later on, he came to know that tempo of accused Kuldeep was falsely implicated in the present accident. Accused was falsely arrested and the present case was registered against him so as to solve this case. He correctly identified the motorcycle in the photograph Ex. P-1 in the testimony of PW-3. 
CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 12 of 17 24. I have heard the arguments addressed by the Learned APP for state and the accused himself and carefully perused the record. 
25.It is argued by the state that prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. Accused was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and caused death of rider and injuries to pillion rider. Tempo has collided with motorcycle and one person has died, res ipsa loquitor is argued by the Ld. APP. 
26.Per contra, it is argued by the Ld. counsel for accused that there are material contradictions in testimony of witnesses. Prosecution has failed to prove rashness and negligence on part of the accused. No public witness is joined by the IO. Eyewitness has deposed falsely at the instance of IO. 
27.I have heard the state and accused and have perused the record carefully. 
28. Allegations against the accused are for offence under section 279/338/304A IPC.
29.Section 279 IPC provides that Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 13 of 17 to one thousand rupees, or with both.
State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
6 30.Section 304 A provides that Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. 
31.In a nutshell to prove the case against the accused the prosecution was under the obligation to prove the following essential ingredients of the offence punishable u/s 279/304A IPC :
a. Identity of the accused being the driver of the offending vehicle. 
b. That the alleged accident is the result of rash and negligent driving of the accused at a public place. c. The rash and negligent driving of the accused resulted in the death of the deceased. 
d. The rash and negligent driving of the accused resulted in the simple injury to the injured. 
32. The question in this case is as to whether, on the evidence on record, it is proved that accused was driving the vehicle and whether he was driving in rash and negligent manner and whether death and injury was caused due to rash and negligent act of the accused. 
33.It was held in Niranjan Singh vs The State (Delhi Administration) 1997 CriLJ 336 that Rashness consists in CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 14 of 17 hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so, and that it may cause injury. The criminality lies in such a case in running the risk of doing such an act with recklessness or indifference as to the consequences. Criminal negligence on the other hand is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable or proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen, it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted. Thus, the main criterion for deciding whether the driving which led to the accident was rash and negligent is not only the speed of the offending vehicle but deliberate disregard to the obligation of its driver to drive with due care and attention and taking a risk indifference as to the harmful consequences resulting from it. In a case of this nature, the test is whether the prosecution has proved that :-
(i) the accused was driving the vehicle in such a manner as to create an obvious and serious risk of causing physical injury to some other person who might happen to be using the road or of doing substantial damage to the property;
(ii) in driving the vehicle in that manner the accused did so without having given any thought to the possibility of there being any such risk or, having recognized that there was some risk involved, had nonetheless gone on to take it; and (iii) the rash or negligent act of the accused was the CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 15 of 17 proximate cause of the death of the deceased.
State vs Kuldeep Singh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88701015/
7 34.In present case it is not disputed that accused was driving the vehicle but that he was driving in rash and negligent manner. In present case prosecution has failed to prove that accused was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner. There is no evidence on record to show that accused was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner. Eye witness PW 7 has only deposed to the effect that offending vehicle was overtaking the vehicle and came from front side and hit the motorcycle. 
However, version of witness do not corroborate with the mechanical inspection report. AS per report offending vehicle was damaged from left side. If accused had overtook the vehicle from right side and hit motorcycle from front then damage should have occurred at right side, and could not have hit the motorcycle at left. As per site plan there is no divider on the place of incident. Traffic direction is not shown on site plan. It is not proved cogently, if accused or injured were on wrong side of the road. PW 11 has stated that vehicle of injured was on wrong side of road. Bald statement of witness that accused was rash and negligent will not ipso facto establish the fact. 
35.It is admitted fact that Tempo stopped at the spot, if it was on very high speed, it would have been difficult to stop the same at the spot after the incident. Further it is nowhere alleged that it was at high speed. Moreover, It is already discussed rashness is not about high speed but total CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 16 of 17 disregard of traffic rules and caution. No such fact is brought on record to show that accused was driving in rash and negligent manner. In the absence of any material on the record, no presumption of "rashness" or "negligence"
could be drawn by invoking the maxim "res ipsa loquitur". 
36. Site plan on record is prepared on the day of incident, and signed by the injured, further IO has stated that he met injured on day of incident at the spot, however, PW 7 in his cross examination has stated that " I left the hospital after two days of incident..........", if witness was in hospital then how hw was present at spot is not explained by the State. 
37.IO has not joined the public witness despite availaibility, notice to join investigation was also not given by the IO to the public, such failure to join public witnesses, cast shadow of doubt on the prosecution case.
38. In such circumstances, it cannot be said that prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. Accordingly, accused Kuldeep Singh is acquitted for offence under section 279/338/304A IPC.

29.Section 279 IPC provides that Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend CC 5283953/16 State Vs.
